title: Protocol to produce high-titer retrovirus for transduction of mouse bone marrow cells
protocol: Seed 6.0 × 10^6 HEK293T cells per 150-mm dish containing 10% FBS in 20 mL high glucose and sodium pyruvate DMEM medium.
Culture the seeded cells for 16-20 hours.
Add 5 mL of fresh warm 293T culture medium containing 1 mM chloroquine to each dish one hour before transfection.
Gently rock the dishes from side to side and return them to the incubator.
Prepare transfection mixture A with 25 μg retroviral plasmid, 20 μg pCL-Eco helper plasmid in 1 mL Opti-MEM.
Prepare transfection mixture B by adding 135 μL of 1 mg/mL PEI to 1 mL Opti-MEM.
Transfer mixture B to A and vortex gently for a short period.
Incubate the transfection mixture for 20 min at 20°C-25°C.
Add 2 mL plasmids/PEI mixture to each 150-mm dish in a dropwise manner.
Rock the dish gently from side to side before returning it to incubator.
Aspirate the old medium after twelve hours of transfection carefully.
Pipette 20 mL fresh 293T medium slowly against the side wall of 150-mm dish.
Return plates to incubator.
Collect supernatant from each 150 mm dish into a 50 mL tube twenty-four hours post medium change.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 10 min at 4°C to remove cells and debris.
Transfer the supernatant carefully into a new 50 mL tube.
Add 1 volume of Retro-X Concentrator for each 3 volumes of supernatant.
Gently mix by inverting the tubes every 10–20 min during the first hour of incubation at 4°C.
Incubate mixture for 10–16 h at 4°C refrigerator.
Centrifuge the samples at 1,500 × g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Discard most of the supernatant.
Add 1/10 to 1/50 of the original volume of RPMI medium with 2% heat-inactivated FBS.
Gently shake the tube on ice until the pellet is completely suspended.
Plate 50,000 healthy NIH 3T3 cells in 500 μL of complete DMEM per well of a 24-well plate.
Return the plate to the incubator and culture for 16–20 hours.
Trypsinize three wells from the plate and count the cell number individually.
Record the average number as (#) cells plated.
Aspirate old medium from each well.
Add 450 μL of complete DMEM containing 8 μg/mL polybrene to each well.
Thaw a vial of frozen retrovirus in a 37°C water bath.
Prepare a series of 10-fold dilutions of the tested virus.
Dilute the viral supernatant with complete DMEM to create a 10^-1 dilution.
Further dilute the 10^-1 solution in complete DMEM to prepare a 10^-2 dilution.
Continue by diluting the 10^-2 solution in complete DMEM to produce a 10^-3 dilution.
Dilute the 10^-3 solution further with complete DMEM to obtain a 10^-4 dilution.
Dispense 50 μL of each viral supernatant dilution into triplicate wells.
Add 50 μL of complete DMEM to three wells as non-viral infection controls.
Gently pipette up and down three times using a 1 mL pipette.
Place the plate back in the incubator for twenty-four hours.
After twenty-four hours, replace the medium containing viral supernatant with fresh complete DMEM (500 μL).
Forty-eight hours post-infection, trypsinize and resuspend cells from each well in FACS buffer individually.
Analyze the percentage of GFP+ cells using a flow cytometer.
Intravenously inject 300 μl of 10 mg/mL 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) into a 20 g adult mouse (150 mg/kg).
Euthanize the mice through cervical dislocation at 4 days after administration of 5-FU.
Rinse the body briefly with 70% ethanol.
Place the mouse on paper towel and transfer it into a biosafety cabinet.
Cut the hind and front limbs into a 100-mm dish containing 10 ml PBS.
Disconnect the joint and remove the muscles as much as possible.
Place the bones in a new 100-mm dish.
Mark cutting sites with red arrows.
Disconnect joints and remove meat from bones.
Transfer clean bones into a new dish.
Flush out bone marrow using a syringe with a 25G 1 1/2 inch needle into a 50 mL tube.
Pipet up and down twice to dissociate cell clumps.
Spin the cells at 400 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Add 5 mL ACK lysis buffer to the cell pellet in a new 15 mL tube.
Resuspend and keep the tube on ice until the lysis is clear.
Add 8 mL flushing buffer to stop lysis, invert the tube 3-5 times.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the bone marrow with 10 mL flushing buffer.
Pass the suspension through a 40 μm strainer to remove tissue and cell clusters.
Enrich c-Kit+ HSPCs using CD117 magnetic beads and LS column (optional).
Centrifuge the sample at 400 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the enriched cells.
Add 1 mL RPMI 1640 medium containing supplements to resuspend HSPCs per mouse in a well of a 6-well plate.
Incubate HSPCs for 20-24 hours in a 37°C incubator supplied with 5% CO2.
Thaw one vial of frozen retrovirus and polybrene in a 37°C water bath.
Add 200 μL of viral suspension and polybrene (final concentration is 8 μg/mL) to one well of a 6-well plate containing 2 mL cell suspension.
Pipette up and down three times to briefly mix the solution.
Incubate the plate in an incubator for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the plate at 500 × g for 90 minutes at 32°C.
Return the plate into the incubator and keep culturing for 2-4 hours.
Repeat spinoculation once by adding 200 μL more concentrated retrovirus to the same well as described above.
Incubate the plate in an incubator for 1-2 hours after the second spinoculation.
Collect cells in a 15 mL tube and count cell number.
Aliquot approximately 10,000 cells in the same medium and keep culture for 24 h.
Check transduction efficiency by FACS if the virus expresses fluorescence (e.g., GFP).
Estimate cell viability by antibiotics resistance gene screening for non-fluorescence expressing virus.
Calculate cell viability as % cell viability = cell (#) after incubation with antibiotics for 24 h / cell plated (#) ×100%.
Wash the cells used for transplantation to remove virus and polybrene with RPMI medium supplied with 2% heat inactivated FBS.
Place the tube on ice until injection into murine recipients.
Perform preliminary experiment to estimate transduction efficiency or measure functional effect through colony formation assay at 24 h after infection.
Transplant bone marrow cells into recipient mouse as early as possible (24–48 h post infection).
Irradiate the recipient mice lethally (1100 Rads, 3 h apart) or sub-lethally (450 Rads once) from an X or gamma irradiator.
Reconstitute irradiated mice into cages with fresh food and drinking water supplied with 0.2 mg/mL Baytril.
Resuspend cells with 10 mL cold RPMI 1640 medium containing 2% heat-inactivated FBS.
Filter the cell suspension through 40 μm strainers.
Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 400 × g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant by vacuum.
Pipette up and down with cells using an appropriate volume of cold RPMI 1640 medium containing 2% heat-inactivated FBS.
Count and adjust cell number to a concentration of 0.2–1 × 10^6 cells/0.2 mL.
Calculate the transduced cell number for each mouse based on the transduction efficiency.
Co-transplant with 0.2–0.5 × 10^5 healthy bone marrow cells as helpers for recipient mice with lethal irradiation.
Inject 0.2 mL of cell suspension into each irradiated recipient mouse via tail vein using a 1.0 mL syringe and 27G 1/2 inch needle.
Change cages with fresh food and drinking water (containing 0.2 mg/mL Baytril) one week post transplantation.
Obtain mononuclear bone marrow cells from each mouse by following the specified protocol.
Intravenously inject 5-FU into mice for HSPC enrichment.
Isolate approximately 5–10 × 10^6 mononuclear BM cells from each mouse four days post-5-FU injection.
Further enrich c-Kit positive BM cells using commercial CD117 magnetic beads.
Pool cells isolated from three mice in one sample.
Transduce pooled cells with retrovirus expressing GFP.
Inject 0.4 × 10^6 transduced cells (CD45.2+) and 0.2 × 10^6 competitor BM cells (CD45.1+) into each irradiated recipient mouse.
